Usage: nc [options] [<host> <port> | <port>]

Cross-platform netcat — TCP/UDP send/receive, port checks, TLS clients.

Options:
  -l, --listen                 Listen for one inbound connection / datagram
  -z, --check                  Check whether port(s) are open and exit
  -u, --udp                    Use UDP (default is TCP)
  --tls                        Wrap TCP connection in TLS (client mode only)
  --insecure                   Skip TLS certificate validation (warning emitted)
  -4, --ipv4                   Force IPv4
  -6, --ipv6                   Force IPv6
  --no-shutdown                Don't half-close socket on stdin EOF
  -v, --verbose                Show closed/timeout ports too in --check mode
  -w, --timeout SEC            Connection / idle timeout in seconds
  --bind ADDR                  Bind listener to specific interface (default: all)
  -h, --help                   Show help
  --version                    Show version
  --no-color                   Disable colored output
  --json                       JSON output
  --describe                   Structured JSON metadata for AI agents
  --color[=auto|always|never]  Coloured output: auto (default when omitted), always, or never

Examples:
  nc -z target.com 443                           Quick port check
  nc -z target.com 80,443,5432                   Check multiple ports
  nc -z target.com 1-1024 --json                 Range check with JSON output
  echo "GET / HTTP/1.0" | nc target.com 80       Send and receive over TCP
  nc --tls api.example.com 443                   TLS client
  nc -u dnsserver 53 < query.bin                 UDP client
  nc -l 8080                                     Listen for one TCP connection on :8080
  nc target.com 80 < request.bin > response.bin  File transfer via piping

Composes with:
  nc -z target 22,80,443 | xargs -I{} echo open: {}           Process open-port list
  retry --until 0 --times 30 --delay 2s nc -z localhost 5432  Wait until a service port accepts connections (wait-for-it replacement)

Exit Codes:
  0
